title: Cross-domain security controls mapping and exception workflow
author: Asha Mehta
body:
Summary:
This document provides a cross-domain mapping of core security and compliance controls (RBAC & auth, audit logging, data residency & retention, secure SDLC, incident response, and compliance evidence workflows) and defines a single exception and risk process for deviations. It is intended for Product, Security, Engineering, SRE, and Compliance teams responsible for implementing or assessing controls.

Purpose and scope:
- Purpose: Reduce duplicate control efforts across teams by standardizing control intent, minimal implementation patterns, monitoring signals, and exception handling.
- Scope: All Redwood-hosted and customer-deployed products (Hosted API, Dedicated, Private) and associated infra components (control plane, serving runtime, data stores, logging pipeline).
- Exclusions: Vendor-managed SaaS where contractual controls replace Redwood implementation — exceptions must be recorded (see Exception Process).

Ownership and SLAs:
- Control owner (security): Security Controls & Compliance Team (owner: Asha Mehta).
- Implementation owners: Service teams (runtime, infra, console, onboardings).
- Review cadence: Quarterly control reviews; RBAC privileged role certification every 90 days.
- Incident SLA (security triage): P1 ack 15 minutes, P1 containment 4 hours; P2 ack 1 hour. Audit evidence requests during audits: initial package within 5 business days.

Controls mapping (high level):
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Control domain           | Purpose                               | Minimal implementation   | Monitoring KPI / Alert threshold                  | Evidence to attach                                   |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| RBAC & Authentication   | Ensure least-privilege access          | Centralized IAM (Okta + internal SCIM); role-based groups; MFA | Quarterly privileged access audit; alert if >1 user added to admin role outside JIT window | Role membership export, access request tickets, JIT logs |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Audit Logging           | Immutable action trail for forensics  | Centralized write-once log stream (kinesis -> elasticsearch -> cold S3) with tamper detection | No drop >0.1% of events per hour; missing critical logs for >15 minutes -> page SRE | Retention policy record, SHA256 manifests, ingestion metrics |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Data Residency & Retention | Ensure data stored within contractual boundaries; minimize retention | Region-tagged storage buckets, encryption-at-rest, configurable retention policies per customer | Any cross-region replication record -> review within 24 hours; retention mis-config -> ticket | Data residency maps, retention config, customer contract clause |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Secure SDLC             | Embed security in CI/CD and releases  | PR gating: SAST, dependency-scan, secret-scan; release checklist; canary rollback | Failed SAST block on merge; secret-scan alert -> immediate rollback and rotation | Scan reports, build artifacts, release notes |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Incident Response       | Rapid detection and response          | Central pager (PagerDuty); triage runbooks; evidence preservation steps | P1 ack >15m -> incident commander escalation to CTO; RKPI: MTTR target <6 hours for infra incidents | Incident timeline export, preserved logs, evidence bundle |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Compliance evidence     | Provide auditors and customers required artifacts | Evidence orchestration: per-audit manifest, automated exports (S3), signed snapshots | Evidence completeness for audit requests: 95% in initial package | Evidence manifests, signatures, change-log |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+

Implementation patterns and examples:

1) RBAC & Auth (implementation pattern)
- Pattern: Centralize identity (Okta) and authorize via a service-level RBAC layer that maps Okta groups to service roles. Use short-lived service tokens with workload identity for intra-cluster auth.
- Privileged access flow: Just-in-time (JIT) elevation via access-request system (request -> approver -> auto-revoke after TTL). TTL defaults: 4 hours for emergency, 1 hour for standard elevated sessions.
- Example IAM snippet (service mapping):

```
# Example role binding (conceptual)
{
  "role": "service-admin",
  "bindings": [
    {"provider": "okta", "group": "redwood:service-admins"}
  ],
  "ttl_seconds": 3600
}
```

- Controls: MFA required for all interactive access; passkeys allowed; CLI tokens rotate every 7 days; service-to-service tokens rotate every 30 days.

2) Audit logging (implementation pattern)
- Pattern: Emit structured JSON events with standardized schema (event_type, actor_id, service, resource_id, request_id, timestamp, outcome). All services append request_id headers for traceability.
- Pipeline: service -> kafka -> log-enrichment -> write-once index -> nearline analytics -> cold S3 (retention tiers). Tamper-detection uses periodic manifest hashes and external signing service (HSM).
- Monitoring: Ingestion lag SLO: 120s (90th percentile). Alert: ingestion_lag >300s for 5m -> page on-call.
- Example event schema (short): {"event_type":"auth.grant","actor_id":"user:123","resource":"project:abc"} (keep as single-line JSON in logs).

3) Data residency & retention
- Pattern: Customer data is tagged at create-time with a residency label. Replication disabled by default across regions unless contract allows. Retention policy engine evaluates object TTL and purges after retention window via scheduled job.
- Retention defaults: logs: 365 days (security-critical) / 90 days (standard); customer PII: per contract (commonly 180 days).
- Implementation note: For Private deployments, retention enforcement must be configured via the on-prem settings during install and verified during pre-flight checks.

4) Secure SDLC
- Gates: PR cannot be merged unless pipeline passes: unit tests, SAST, dependency-check, secret-scan. Build artifacts are signed using CI key (rotated quarterly). Release checklist includes: security changelog, rollback instructions, canary percentage, and monitored metrics.
- Canary rollout: default 5% for 2 hours, metrics stable -> 25% for 6 hours -> global. Automatic rollback triggers: error-rate increase >2x baseline AND latency p95 increase >30% during canary window.

5) Incident response security procedures
- On detection: create incident in tracking system (link to runbook), preserve evidence snapshot (logs, VM/docker images metadata, audit stream snapshot).
- For suspected data exfiltration: isolate affected instances, snapshot disks, export logs to immutable store, and notify legal and customer success within 24 hours if contractual breach likely.
- Evidence preservation steps (quick):
  1. Capture timestamps and request_ids.
  2. Lock log write permissions to prevent rotation/overwrite.
  3. Create read-only artifacts in signed S3 with SHA256 manifest.

Exception and risk handling workflow (single canonical process)
1. Request: Service owner files an Exception Request ticket in JIRA with template fields: affected_control, justification, compensating_controls, duration, owner, rollback_condition.
2. Initial review (48 hours): Security triage validates completeness.
3. Risk assessment (5 business days): Security + Infra + Product review residual risk and required compensating controls.
4. Approval: For <30 days, Security Approver may approve. >30 days or cross-region/data-residency exceptions require CISO and Legal sign-off.
5. Mitigations & monitoring: All approved exceptions must have monitoring (alerting thresholds) and a mitigation plan documented. Exceptions are timeboxed and auto-expire.
6. Renewal: Requests to renew must submit 7 business days before expiry; renewals get expedited review but require fresh justification.

Exception decision template (fields):
- id: EXC-2025-####
- service: (service name)
- scope: (controls and resources)
- risk_summary: (text)
- compensating_controls: (list)
- approved_by: (names)
- expires_on: (YYYY-MM-DD)

Operational checklist for auditors / evidence packaging
- Assemble: control mapping matrix (this doc), implementation evidence (config exports), logs (signed manifests), role membership exports, JIT audit log, release artifacts for the period under review.
- Packaging steps (CLI examples):
  1. Export roles: `tools/iam/export-roles --service runtime --out roles.csv`
  2. Snapshot logs: `tools/logs/snapshot --since 2025-08-01 --until 2025-08-31 --sign --out s3://evidence/2025-08-logs`
  3. Generate manifest: `tools/evidence/manifest --path s3://evidence/2025-08-logs > manifest.json`

Change log and governance
- Changes to this mapping require sign-off from Security and at least one impacted service owner. Major changes (affecting residency, retention, or RBAC model) must be communicated two weeks prior to enforcement via company-wide digest and product release notes.

Appendix: Quick reference snippets
- RBAC review schedule (example):
  - Day 0: export admin roles -> Day 7: security review -> Day 10: owner remediation ticket -> Day 30: closure.
- Audit ingestion SLOs: 90th percentile ingestion <120s; error budget: <0.1% lost events/month.

Contact and escalation
- Security controls owner: Asha Mehta (ashamehta@redwood.ai)
- On-call security (PagerDuty): sec-oncall@redwood.ai (see internal rota)
- Legal escalation: legal-escalations@redwood.ai

Note: This is a living document; teams implementing these patterns should attach concrete implementation pages under the service subspace and link back to this canonical mapping.
